title: Cross-SDK retry blueprint: defaults, idempotency keys, stream resume
creator: Aisha Khatri
description:
Summary: Define a clear, cross-language default for retry/backoff behavior, idempotency key contract, and streaming resume ergonomics for Redwood SDKs (Python/TypeScript/Go). This ticket produces a single playbook that SDKs implement and a small set of helper primitives (IdempotencyKey helper, RetryPolicy object, StreamResume helper).

Background and motivation: Teams repeatedly implement bespoke retry logic which leads to inconsistent behavior across languages and customer pain (either overly aggressive retries that double-charge or under-retrying that surface transient errors). Streaming introduces additional complexity: long-lived connections, partial outputs, and the need for consistent resume semantics. We need an operationally safe, pragmatic, and simple contract that SDK users can rely on.

Goals:
- Define default retryable error taxonomy (HTTP status codes, transport errors) shared across SDKs.
- Standardize exponential backoff + jitter defaults and provide one-step opt-in presets (conservative, aggressive, throughput-optimized).
- Define idempotency key contract: header name, recommended client generation, server dedup window, expected server responses, and TTL.
- Provide streaming resume pattern: checkpointing API surface, header semantics for server-provided resume tokens, and fallback behavior when resume is unavailable.
- Provide language-specific examples for Python, TypeScript, and Go and hooks for advanced users.

Design decisions and recommended defaults:
- Retryable status codes: 429, 502, 503, 504 should be retried by default. 500 is NOT retried by default (requires classification).
- Transport errors: connection reset, connection refused, read/write timeouts, DNS resolution failures are retryable. SDKs should map their native error types to the taxonomy.
- Idempotency header: X-Idempotency-Key (RFC-like but simple). Clients MAY send; server deduplication is best-effort for 24 hours by default. Recommended server response on duplicate: 409 with X-Dedup-Status: duplicate (or 200/201 with same resource id if operation completed). SDKs should surface a Deduplication object when available.
- Idempotency key generation: SDK helpers expose IdempotencyKey.v4() that generates a UUIDv4 and optionally tags with operation type. Document guidance: keys should be client-generated for operations that mutate state (create, mutate) and omitted for pure read/generate calls unless the user explicitly wants dedup.
- Backoff defaults: exponential backoff with base_delay=200ms, multiplier=2.0, max_delay=10s, max_retries=5. Use full jitter (per AWS best practices). Provide presets: conservative (max_retries=3, max_delay=5s), default (as above), aggressive (max_retries=8, base_delay=100ms, max_delay=20s).
- Retry budget: SDKs should respect a per-request overall timeout and use a retry budget so retries do not exceed the overall deadline.

Streaming ergonomics:
- Resume token header: server MAY return X-Stream-Resume-Token at chunk boundaries and on finalization. The SDK should surface a StreamCheckpoint object to users.
- Checkpointing API: SDKs expose a simple on_chunk(callback) where the callback receives (chunk, optional_resume_token) and SDK persists resume token automatically if user opts-in via auto_resume=true.
- Resume semantics: when a stream connection is interrupted and a valid resume token is available, SDKs attempt a single resume request to the same model/route. Resume requests are idempotent only when client supplies the original Idempotency-Key or the server explicitly marks the resume operation as safe. If resume fails, SDK falls back to a full restart and provides both partial and retry outputs to the application.
- Non-resumable streams: any stream that invokes external tools or has side-effectful outcomes must be considered non-resumable by default unless the server documents explicit resume guarantees.

Examples (high-level snippets included for all three SDKs):
- Python: RetryPolicy class + decorator @retryable_request(policy=RetryPolicy.default()) and IdempotencyKey helper. Example shows embedding create call with IdempotencyKey: idempotency = IdempotencyKey.v4(); client.create_embedding(..., idempotency_key=idempotency).
- TypeScript: client.withRetryPolicy(RetryPresets.default).createCompletion({ prompt }, { idempotencyKey }). SDK exposes stream.on('chunk', handler) and stream.checkpoint() that returns a resumeToken.
- Go: Functional options on client.NewRequest(WithRetry(RetryPolicyDefault), WithIdempotencyKey(key)). StreamResume helper returns a token string and SaveResumeToken(ctx, token) helper.

Testing and validation:
- Create a small e2e harness that injects transient errors and verifies deduplication: simulate server responses 503 then 200 and ensure SDK retry behavior.
- Streaming harness to drop connection mid-stream and validate resume token flow and fallback to restart.
- Unit tests for mapping native network errors to retryable taxonomy.

Migration path:
- Implement in SDKs behind a feature flag for two release cycles.
- Add telemetry: counts of retries, idempotency key usage rate, resume successes/failures.
- Communicate breaking behavior (e.g., default not to retry HTTP 500) in migration notes and SDK changelogs.

Operational notes:
- Server-side: maintain deduplication window metadata (24h default) and expose admin endpoint to evict keys.
- Logs: when dedup detected, log idempotency key and original operation idempotency_result to enable debugging.

Open questions / trade-offs:
- Dedup window duration trade-off between storage cost and safety (propose 24h but allow org-level override).
- Whether to treat 500 as retryable for model server transient failures; short-term opt-in via RetryPresets.aggressive.
- Exact wire semantics for stream resume (token format) — propose opaque base64 token; server owns schema.

Deliverables:
- This playbook (this ticket).
- SDK helper implementations in python, ts, go (3 PRs).
- e2e harness + CI jobs.
- Confluence page for runtime/ops configuration and support runbook.
acceptance_criteria: 1) SDKs (Python/TS/Go) implement RetryPolicy with shared defaults and expose presets. 2) IdempotencyKey helper available and documented with examples. 3) Stream clients expose checkpoint/resume primitives and a documented fallback behavior. 4) Unit and e2e tests for retry taxonomy and streaming resume exist and pass in CI. 5) Telemetry emitted for retries/idempotency/resume and dashboards created.

2026-03-04: Initial Python prototype PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-python/pull/412 — implements RetryPolicy and IdempotencyKey helper. Requesting design review from @lucy and @mohit.
2026-03-06: Decision: default list of retryable HTTP codes set to [429,502,503,504]. 500 excluded by default after PM input (avoids masking logical model errors).
2026-03-07: UX note from Design (Carla Mendes): suggested stream checkpoint surface should be minimal (on_chunk + optional auto_persist flag). Implementation adjusted accordingly.
2026-03-09: Added streaming e2e harness PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-integration-tests/pull/78 — simulates TCP resets and validates resume tokens.
2026-03-10: Security review flagged storage of idempotency keys for PII considerations; security_review_required set to true and follow-up ticket created (ENG-551235).
